    12  /-!
    13  # Closure operators between preorders
    14  
    15  We define (bundled) closure operators on a preorder as monotone (increasing), extensive
    16  (inflationary) and idempotent functions.
    17  We define closed elements for the operator as elements which are fixed by it.
    18  
    19  Lower adjoints to a function between preorders `u : β → α` allow to generalise closure operators to
    20  situations where the closure operator we are dealing with naturally decomposes as `u ∘ l` where `l`
    21  is a worthy function to have on its own. Typical examples include
    22  `l : Set G → Subgroup G := Subgroup.closure`, `u : Subgroup G → Set G := (↑)`, where `G` is a group.
    23  This shows there is a close connection between closure operators, lower adjoints and Galois
    24  connections/insertions: every Galois connection induces a lower adjoint which itself induces a
    25  closure operator by composition (see `GaloisConnection.lowerAdjoint` and
    26  `LowerAdjoint.closureOperator`), and every closure operator on a partial order induces a Galois
    27  insertion from the set of closed elements to the underlying type (see `ClosureOperator.gi`).
    28  
    29  ## Main definitions
    30  
    31  * `ClosureOperator`: A closure operator is a monotone function `f : α → α` such that
    32    `∀ x, x ≤ f x` and `∀ x, f (f x) = f x`.
    33  * `LowerAdjoint`: A lower adjoint to `u : β → α` is a function `l : α → β` such that `l` and `u`
    34    form a Galois connection.
    35  
    36  ## Implementation details
    37  
    38  Although `LowerAdjoint` is technically a generalisation of `ClosureOperator` (by defining
    39  `toFun := id`), it is desirable to have both as otherwise `id`s would be carried all over the
    40  place when using concrete closure operators such as `ConvexHull`.
    41  
    42  `LowerAdjoint` really is a semibundled `structure` version of `GaloisConnection`.
    43  
    44  ## References
    45  
    46  * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closure_operator#Closure_operators_on_partially_ordered_sets
    47  -/
    48  
    49  @[expose] public section
    50  
    51  open Set

    56  variable (α : Type*) {ι : Sort*} {κ : ι → Sort*}
    57  
    58  /-- A closure operator on the preorder `α` is a monotone function which is extensive (every `x`
    59  is less than its closure) and idempotent. -/
    60  structure ClosureOperator [Preorder α] extends α →o α where
    61    /-- An element is less than or equal its closure -/
    62    le_closure' : ∀ x, x ≤ toFun x
    63    /-- Closures are idempotent -/
    64    idempotent' : ∀ x, toFun (toFun x) = toFun x
    65    /-- Predicate for an element to be closed.
    66  
    67    By default, this is defined as `c.IsClosed x := (c x = x)` (see `isClosed_iff`).
    68    We allow an override to fix definitional equalities. -/
    69    IsClosed (x : α) : Prop := toFun x = x
    70    isClosed_iff {x : α} : IsClosed x ↔ toFun x = x := by aesop

    72  namespace ClosureOperator

    78  instance [Preorder α] : OrderHomClass (ClosureOperator α) α α where
    79    map_rel f _ _ h := f.mono h

    11  /-!
    12  # Nucleus
    13  
    14  Locales are the dual concept to frames. Locale theory is a branch of point-free topology, where
    15  intuitively locales are like topological spaces which may or may not have enough points.
    16  Sublocales of a locale generalize the concept of subspaces in topology to the point-free setting.
    17  
    18  A nucleus is an endomorphism of a frame which corresponds to a sublocale.
    19  
    20  ## References
    21  https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/sublocale
    22  https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/nucleus
    23  -/
    24  
    25  @[expose] public section
    26  
    27  open Order InfHom Set
    28  
    29  variable {X : Type*}
    30  
    31  /-- A nucleus is an inflationary idempotent `inf`-preserving endomorphism of a semilattice.
    32  
    33  In a frame, nuclei correspond to sublocales. See `nucleusIsoSublocale`. -/
    34  structure Nucleus (X : Type*) [SemilatticeInf X] extends InfHom X X where
    35    /-- A nucleus is idempotent.
    36  
    37    Do not use this directly. Instead use `NucleusClass.idempotent`. -/
    38    idempotent' (x : X) : toFun (toFun x) ≤ toFun x
    39    /-- A nucleus is increasing.
    40  
    41    Do not use this directly. Instead use `NucleusClass.le_apply`. -/
    42    le_apply' (x : X) : x ≤ toFun x
    43  
    44  /-- `NucleusClass F X` states that F is a type of nuclei. -/
    45  class NucleusClass (F X : Type*) [SemilatticeInf X] [FunLike F X X] : Prop
    46      extends InfHomClass F X X where
    47    /-- A nucleus is idempotent. -/
    48    idempotent (x : X) (f : F) : f (f x) ≤ f x
    49    /-- A nucleus is inflationary. -/
    50    le_apply (x : X) (f : F) : x ≤ f x
